title: Contract Pricing Agreement Contract Administration Note: Protected Price of a Substitute
content:
Contract administration note — protected price of a substitute (Contract Pricing Agreement)

**Substitute in view.** The Corbett-approved substitute that filled the latest backorder on the customer's ship-tos (as the customer's Ship-To Fulfillment Account records show it) for a contract item of another item number (one for which the agreement carries an added price line), when the agreement carries no price line for the substitute's item number yet. The line is effective on the discontinuation date, the ship date of that substitute fill. Calendar days from one date to another count the later date and not the earlier one. Wherever a latest or most recent record of a kind is taken, it is the one with the latest date, and among records of the same date the one recorded first.

**Protected price.** The protected price is the contract unit price that ends on the discontinued item's close-out line (the removal line recorded for the discontinued item on the agreement's contract item list); it is rounded half up to four decimal places once, on the final figure. The concessions set for the protection are added together and taken off the protected price once, before that rounding.

**Worked example (hypothetical).** The discontinued item's close-out line records 12.3400 as the contract unit price that ends; the substitute's protection line is added effective on the substitute fill's ship date at 12.3400.
